RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Reese Kimura
Member ID: W325265581
Reference Number: POC-BF385BB269-48000
Date of Notice: 2026-08-14
Denied Service: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus correction), CPT 28296
Requesting Provider: Dr. Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Grievance and Appeals Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296 (correction, hallux valgus with bunionectomy), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-14. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure."

Important note on the basis for this appeal: The denial notice does not cite a specific medical policy title, policy number, or clinical criteria document, and CountyCare has not provided me with the text of the criteria it applied. I have reviewed CountyCare's publicly available list of clinical policies for prior authorization and was unable to locate any policy specific to foot surgery, bunionectomy, or hallux valgus correction (CPT 28296). Accordingly, I am not able to quote or respond point-by-point to specific plan criteria language, because none has been disclosed to me, and I have not invented or assumed any such language. I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that CountyCare provide in writing the exact name, number, and text of the medical necessity criteria applied to this denial, including any InterQual, MCG, or other licensed clinical guideline relied upon, so that I and my surgeon may respond to it directly if this appeal is not resolved in my favor.

In the absence of disclosed criteria, I am presenting, in my own words, the clinical evidence in my chart that I believe supports medical necessity for this procedure, directly addressing the stated concern that the imaging did not support the request:

1. Imaging findings. Weight-bearing radiographs of the foot obtained on 2026-07-11 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees. These are well outside normal limits (normal hallux valgus angle is generally considered under 15 degrees and normal intermetatarsal angle under 9 degrees) and reflect a moderate-to-severe structural bunion deformity. I ask that CountyCare's reviewing physician re-examine these specific measurements, as I believe the denial rationale that "imaging findings do not support medical necessity" does not accurately reflect the degree of deformity documented.

2. Failed conservative treatment. I completed a supervised course of conservative care, including activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic, over 10 weeks (2026-05-06 through 2026-07-15), completing 16 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also completed 4 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-02 that provided only 3 weeks of partial relief. This represents a substantial, well-documented trial of non-surgical management that has failed to resolve my symptoms.

3. Duration and severity of symptoms. I have experienced 12 months of progressive foot pain that is unrelieved by rest, indicating a chronic and worsening condition rather than a transient complaint.

4. Functional impairment and risk. I am currently unable to tolerate closed shoes because of the bunion prominence, and there is a documented risk of skin ulceration over the prominence. On examination, I have a positive provocative test on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion at the first metatarsophalangeal joint. These findings demonstrate a functional impairment and an emerging medical risk (ulceration) beyond cosmetic concern.

5. Absence of contraindications. I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker, none of which should present a barrier to surgical candidacy.

Taken together, the severity of the radiographic deformity (38-degree hallux valgus angle, 17-degree intermetatarsal angle), the 12-month symptom duration, the documented failure of a comprehensive conservative treatment trial (orthotics, footwear modification, 16 physical therapy visits, 4 months of NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection), and the functional impairment with ulceration risk together support that CPT 28296 is medically necessary. I respectfully ask that CountyCare's appeal reviewer reconsider the denial in light of this full clinical picture, and that any adverse decision on appeal identify with specificity which criteria in the applicable medical policy are not met by these findings.

Timeliness of this appeal: The denial notice states that an appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date (by 2027-02-10). I note that this appears to differ from the 60-calendar-day appeal window described in CountyCare's own published Member Rights & Appeals materials. Because I am uncertain which deadline governs my situation, I am submitting this appeal well within either timeframe, and I ask CountyCare to confirm in writing which appeal deadline applies to this determination. I also request that CountyCare confirm whether I am entitled to request continuation of my current authorization status while this appeal is pending, and by what date any such request must be made.

Enclosed with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting the conservative treatment course (2026-05-06 to 2026-07-15, 16 visits)
- Weight-bearing foot radiograph report dated 2026-07-11 (hallux valgus angle 38°, intermetatarsal angle 17°)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-06-02)
- Office examination notes documenting provocative testing, range of motion, and ulceration risk
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor, MD [to be attached]
- [Any additional records the surgeon's office identifies]

Please notify me and Dr. Okafor's office in writing of the outcome of this appeal, and please provide the specific policy or clinical criteria document relied upon in any further determination, consistent with my right to understand and respond to the basis for any denial.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Reese Kimura
